cognate: ON eiga (Gmc *aigan, perfect-present) = Ved. īś- 'be master of', both *h₂eyḱ-; ON fé = Ved. paśu-, both *péḱu
drift_or_renewal: ON fé drifted from 'livestock' to 'property, money' (cf. Lat. pecunia); ON eiga is 'own' where Ved. īś- is 'have power over, rule'
shared_syntax: subject (lord/king) + *h₂eyḱ- verb + *péḱu as its object (ON acc.; Ved. genitive of rule)
context: who is owner/master of the (live) wealth: ON law gives confiscated goods to the king (konungr á þat fé); AV addresses the god as lord of the beasts (tvam īśiṣe paśūnām). In the search index *péḱu is the second-strongest collocate of *h₂eyḱ- in both branches (Indo-Iranian 13 units, O/E 5.8; Germanic 236, O/E 2.7).

search_lead.cognate: ON ljós (*léwk-s-) ~ Lat. lūmen (*léwk-s-mn̥); Greek renews with φάος (*bʰeh₂-)
search_lead.argument: 'come/be brought into the light' = 'be born': ON law kømr lífi í ljós (a child 'comes alive into the light', i.e. born alive) matches Ennian-Lucretian in luminis oras (of birth, in the same directional 'into' construction) with a cognate *lewk-s- noun, and Homer's birth-goddess formula πρὸ φόως ἐξάγαγε with a renewed light-word. Caveat: Christian/Latin 'in lucem venire' may lie behind the ON legal phrase.

near_miss.lead: ON í heyranda hljóði (*h₂ḱh₂ows- + *ḱlew-) ~ Gk ἀκοῇ τε κλύειν (*h₂ḱh₂ows- + *ḱlew-)
near_miss.why_not: Two 'hear' roots side by side in both, but ON is the legal 'in public hearing' formula and Sophocles is 'hear with the ears' paired with 'see a sight'; Greek pair hits are almost all κλέος ἀκούειν 'hear fame', a different figure. Pleonasm of near-synonyms, likely independent.

near_miss.lead: poet 'makes' praise: MW gwneuthum ... glot ... gwawt ~ ON hefir ort ... hljóðum, Óðins (*weh₂t- poetry word in both)
near_miss.why_not: Welsh verb is not *werǵ- (see error line), ON hljóð is not 'fame' here, and Óðinn is a name; the *weh₂tu- 'poetry' isogloss is lexical, not a shared phrase.

near_miss.lead: woman given in marriage under father, brother, mother (ON giftingarmaðr list) ~ AV bride 'bound in the house of mother, brother, father'
near_miss.why_not: Same three cognate kin terms in a marriage context, but listing kin is generic and the order and function differ (legal guardians vs. the bride's natal house).

near_miss.lead: merism of booty/killing: Ir. cach bó cach ben ~ ON karlla oc konur oc born oc fenuð (cf. Umbr. viro pequo)
near_miss.why_not: Only ben/kona cognate; the *wiHro-*peḱu merism words are absent; enumeration of living things in a raid is generic.

near_miss.lead: ON (með) orðum eða verkum 'by word or deed' (*werdʰom + *werǵom)
near_miss.why_not: Pair occurs only in Germanic in the index (no Italic/Greek pair hits); likely Christian 'verbo et opere' calque; no cross-branch partner.

near_miss.lead: ON oath satt segja 'say the truth'; guð hollr ... gramr
near_miss.why_not: Partner is a chronicle note on thunder (гром ~ gramr is a false link); 'tell truth' with *h₁sont- + *sekʷ- is only Germanic here.

near_miss.lead: proverb 'where I see the ears I expect the wolf' (cf. Lat. lupus in fabula / auribus teneo lupum)
near_miss.why_not: Greek partner has only a name Λύκος; Latin proverbs differ in sense; no shared wording.

near_miss.lead: wolf + *bʰeyd- (ON úlfr beit ~ Skt bhittvā ... vṛkāṇām)
near_miss.why_not: ON 'bite' vs Skt 'split' wolves' bodies (Kaca bursting out); different agent/patient roles, chance.

near_miss.lead: sleeping draught: Ir. deug suain ~ ON druckin ... sofnaði
near_miss.why_not: Only the sleep root is shared; drink words not cognate; generic narrative.

near_miss.lead: 'mother's sister' (siur a máthar ~ móðir mín er systir hans)

error.correct_reading: áille, pl. of álainn 'beautiful' (neoil áilli aen-gela 'beautiful bright clouds'); not ail 'rock'
machad 'milking-yard, cattle-enclosure' (cá lias cá machad 'whether fold or milking-yard'); no PIE *ped- (that gives Ir. ed-)
error.evidence: context pairs it with lias 'fold, hut' among bó

error.correct_reading: MW gwneuthur/gwnaf belongs with OIr. gniid 'does' (Celtic *gni-), not *werǵ-
error.evidence: recalled; Celtic *werǵ- gives OIr. fairggid/do-ingair-type forms, not W gwna-

error.correct_reading: personal name Úlfr (Ulfr var maðr auðigr)
error.evidence: subject of a man's description; also Ulfs son patronymics in Njáls saga 37r:12 and 40r:16

error.correct_reading: personal name Lykos in a genealogy (Γνούρου τοῦ Λύκου)
